_comment: Example per-board analysis config for a hypothetical board: a 12 V input on J1 (net VIN) through fuse F1 onto +12V, which feeds output connectors J2-J5 and a 5 V buck U2 (output inductor L1); a 3.3 V buck U3 (output inductor L2) feeds the MCU U1 and a radio module U4. Every ref, pad and net here is a placeholder: replace them with your own board's, after reading netlist.md, and delete entries that do not apply. Regexes match KiCad net names exactly as they appear in netlist.md (sheet-local nets look like /Power/NAME); the first matching rule wins. Power runs: the source pad is held at 0 V and each sink draws its amps; negative amps inject current (ground returns). Optional per run: h (grid pitch, mm) and region [x0, y0, x1, y1] (only copper inside the box is solved). rail_voltages gives the voltage of rails whose name does not contain it. diff_pairs: {"nets": [P, N], "target_ohm": differential impedance} or the short form [P, N] (no target); other keys are an error. thermal: the heat-source table and the thermal solve (format in scripts/heat.py). Corners name the operating points that bound the heat; a current is a number, a name defined in the corner, {"run": power run} or {"path_budget": a file written by pcb-power-supply path_budget.py --json, "source", "R_corner"}. Any value can be per corner ({"full_load": x}); a corner missing from such a dict is UNKNOWN there. psi_jb / theta_jc and the limits come from each part's datasheet; the numbers below are illustrative, not data.
